preview_text: UK vacancies have fallen to their lowest outside the pandemic since 2014, and REC finds UK employers' permanent hiring intentions edging down. Talent engineering is the argument of the week, from a Zapier talent engineer's case for buying over building to Data Driven Recruiter asking whether the job is real. Pin and Teamtailor ship AI that acts on candidates for you, while Dayforce is buying AI interviewing firm Ribbon AI. And in the world of AI, a Figma product manager runs his day from shared AI skills, and Kevin Roose had a council of Claude agents review his book.
preview_check: Every topic in the preview must appear in the items below. Recruiting-side topics: ONS vacancies (ONS), REC hiring intentions (REC), talent engineering (Building the Talent Machine, Data Driven Recruiter), Pin Autopilot and Teamtailor Smart action, Dayforce/Ribbon AI. Closing AI sentence: How I AI Figma PM, AI & I Kevin Roose.

items.title: How to Automate Hiring Launches (Claude + Slack)
items.guest_line: Emily Paik · Senior People Operations Manager @ Kit
bullets: At Kit, opening a role used to mean the same 30 minutes of manual busywork every time, so Emily Paik replaced it with a single Slack command.
Paik's Slack form offers three options in Ashby: create a new opening, link the job to an opening pre-created for headcount planning with finance, or create the job only.
Every new role at Kit gets a Slack channel named by rule: engineering roles carry the squad name and contract roles get a contract prefix.

items.title: How to Use Claude for Talent Acquisition
bullets: Adriano Herdman gives Claude the intake call transcript and job spec, connected to Clay, and gets back six profiles across three tiers for hiring manager calibration.
Herdman says his intake calibration skill in Claude cut time to alignment with hiring managers from 24 hours to as little as 10 minutes.
One panellist says Exa's free plan is enough to source up to about 50 to 100 profiles a day when connected to Claude.

items.title: Six Predictions For AI In HR
items.guest_line: Vik Kohli · Head of AI Transformation and People Strategy @ Cloudflare
bullets: Vik Kohli judges AI on several dimensions of value, such as scale, quality and risk mitigation, rather than on time saved alone.
Kohli's most controversial prediction is that staff will hide their AI use, because doing more work with AI just earns them more work.
With candidate AI and employer AI now talking to each other, Kohli expects a small live project during the interview to become the default way to assess capability.

items.title: Talent Engineering Hard Truths
items.guest_line: Dan McCarthy · Senior Talent Engineer @ Zapier
bullets: Zapier talent engineer Dan McCarthy will not rebuild enterprise tools such as Juicebox, Metaview or Pin, because he says he would not build them better.
Before building any recruiting tool, McCarthy asks who the stakeholders are, who will maintain it and what the security risks are.
McCarthy's goal for automation is more time with people: 90 minutes with every candidate before offer, instead of 30.

standout.name: Building the Talent Machine, Talent Engineering Hard Truths (Dan McCarthy)
standout.why: Zapier's senior talent engineer will not rebuild tools like Juicebox, Metaview or Pin, and asks who will maintain any tool before it gets built. Run that check before your team starts its next automation project.

items.title: Halving Attrition With a Connected Career Framework
items.guest_line: Nic Weatherhead · Global Vice President of People @ The Stepstone Group
bullets: Stepstone's career framework describes every role by scope, knowledge, autonomy and complexity, and it was piloted on the recruitment team first.
Where someone sat in a bigger or smaller role than expected, Stepstone left their pay unchanged and built a pathway to the right level instead.
Nic Weatherhead says AI agents change what autonomy means in a role, with less supervising of people and more verifying of information.

items.title: Is Talent Engineering Bullshit?
bullets: Metaview has split TA into three seats, with Talent Engineers covering AI, automation and building alongside Talent Partners and Talent Ops.
Pave did not class Talent Engineer as an established new job, grouping it with Marketing Engineer and Legal Engineer as a re-designed role.
The author's test for whether a talent engineer is still a recruiter: will they own any reqs and be accountable for hiring them?

items.title: Why an Anthropic hiring leader dropped coding tests
bullets: Felix Rieseberg, a hiring manager at Anthropic, says that this month he laid the traditional coding interview to rest.
30% of EU job ads now show a salary range, up from 2% in 2022, according to Revelio Labs figures cited in the issue.
In vendor research from iCIMS and Kyle & Co. covering 500 leaders, the average organisation puts only about half its purchased AI into production.

items.title: Every Dead Link in Your Outreach Is a Candidate You Paid For and Lost
bullets: Over 12 months, 232 people clicked one agency's outreach links to jobs that no longer existed: 14% of the 1,657 people contacted.
After that agency redirected its dead job links, 31 people ended up in its ATS, 13 became active candidates and 2 were hired.
Pew found that a quarter of web pages from 2013 to 2023 were no longer accessible by October 2023.

items.title: Your Talent Insights from Ashby This Month
bullets: Inbound applications made up more than half of hires at Ashby customers by Q1 2026, at 54.3% in EMEA and 51.9% in AMER.
Across Ashby customers, only 28% of inbound hires receive the top quality of hire score, compared with 36% of referral hires.
From July 2027, California's No Robo Bosses Act stops employers relying solely on AI to discipline or fire someone, so a person must check its output.

items.title: How good are your recruiters at spotting talent?
bullets: TA Unboxed proposes an Early Talent Recognition Rate: how often a recruiter flagged the eventual hire as Standout before the first interview.
In the issue's worked example, two recruiters both spot 75% of eventual hires, but the one using half as many Standout flags gives the stronger signal.
Date-stamp every Standout flag and record the stage, so nobody can reach offer stage and claim they knew the candidate was brilliant all along.

standout.name: TA Unboxed, How good are your recruiters at spotting talent?
standout.why: Add one date-stamped Standout flag at CV review and screening, then measure how often each recruiter flagged the eventual hire before the first interview. It turns gut feel about talent spotting into a number.

items.section: Recruiting reports, product updates, and more
items.title: Labour market overview, UK: October 2026
bullets: UK vacancies fell to 691,000 in July to September 2026, the lowest outside the Covid period since July to September 2014.
UK payrolled employees fell by 111,000 (0.4%) between August 2025 and August 2026, according to ONS.
UK regular pay growth excluding bonuses was 3.7% in June to August 2026, with private sector regular pay growth at 3.0%.

standout.name: ONS Labour market overview, UK: October 2026
standout.why: UK vacancies fell to 691,000 in July to September 2026, the lowest outside the pandemic since 2014 and down 37,000 on the year, a UK number worth quoting in your next workforce planning conversation.

items.section: Recruiting reports, product updates, and more
items.title: JobsOutlook, June to August 2026
bullets: In REC's survey of 704 UK employers, economic confidence rose eight points to a net balance of -39% in June to August 2026.
UK employers' confidence in making hiring and investment decisions improved by six points to a net balance of -8%.
Short-term permanent hiring intentions among UK employers edged down one point to a net balance of +8%.

items.section: Recruiting reports, product updates, and more
items.title: Autopilot
bullets: Pin's Autopilot takes over the conversation once a candidate replies, answering questions, booking interviews and updating pipeline stages.
Teams can start with Autopilot drafts they review, or let it answer, book and follow up on its own, set team-wide or per job.
When Autopilot does not know an answer, Pin says it checks with the recruiter on Slack instead of guessing.

standout.name: Pin, Autopilot
standout.why: Once a candidate replies, Pin's Autopilot answers their questions and books the interview, and it checks with you on Slack when it does not know an answer. Teams can start on drafts they review before letting it run alone.

items.section: Recruiting reports, product updates, and more
items.title: Smart action
bullets: Teamtailor's Smart action lets a recruiter describe a task in plain language, then AI applies it to every candidate who enters that stage.
Smart action only uses what a recruiter on the job would see, such as the CV and application answers, and leaves the record unchanged when information is missing.
Before a Smart action prompt is saved, a Verify check warns if the request could lead to biased decisions.

items.title: The Inside Story of the 50 Who Built Modern AI
bullets: Kevin Roose had a council of Claude agents with personas, such as an AI sceptic and an AI historian, review each chapter draft of his book.
Roose says his agent council caught a couple of factual errors that he and his human editors had missed.
Roose keeps 'weightlifting' tasks, where the struggle is part of the benefit, and hands other work such as company paperwork to AI.

items.title: The AI chief of staff that this Figma PM uses all day
items.guest_line: Ezra Mechaber · Growth Product Manager @ Figma
bullets: Figma keeps its 60 to 70 product managers roughly in sync with one shared, automatically updated set of AI skills.
Ezra Mechaber runs a 'what's up' skill about six times a day, pulling Slack and project context into a priority list.
When an AI assistant starts looping, Mechaber assumes the conversation's context is poisoned and simply starts a new conversation.

standout.name: How I AI, The AI chief of staff that this Figma PM uses all day (Ezra Mechaber)
standout.why: Figma keeps 60 to 70 product managers roughly in sync with one shared set of AI skills, a setup a TA ops team could copy for its own prompts and workflows.

items.title: Dayforce agrees to acquire Ribbon AI
bullets: Dayforce has agreed to acquire Toronto-based Ribbon AI, and neither the purchase price nor the closing date was disclosed.
Ribbon runs voice and video AI interviews around the clock, with questions and scoring rubrics generated from the job description.
Once the deal completes, Ribbon's technology will be built natively into Dayforce's new Agentic Recruiting experience.
